            content: Full content of the file.

        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

class Span(NamedTuple):
    """A marked up region in some text."""

    start: int
    """Span start index."""
    end: int
    """Span end index."""
    style: Union[str, Style]
    """Style associated with the span."""

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Span({self.start}, {self.end}, {self.style!r})"

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return self.end > self.start

    def split(self, offset: int) -> Tuple["Span", Optional["Span"]]:
        """Split a span in to 2 from a given offset."""

        if offset < self.start:
            return self, None
        if offset >= self.end:
            return self, None

        start, end, style = self
        span1 = Span(start, min(end, offset), style)
        span2 = Span(span1.end, end, style)
        return span1, span2

    def move(self, offset: int) -> "Span":
        """Move start and end by a given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): Number of characters to add to start and end.

        Returns:
            TextSpan: A new TextSpan with adjusted position.
        """
        start, end, style = self
        return Span(start + offset, end + offset, style)

    def right_crop(self, offset: int) -> "Span":
        """Crop the span at the given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): A value between start and end.

        Returns:
            Span: A new (possibly smaller) span.
        """
        start, end, style = self
        if offset >= end:
            return self
        return Span(start, min(offset, end), style)

    def extend(self, cells: int) -> "Span":
        """Extend the span by the given number of cells.

        Args:
            cells (int): Additional space to add to end of span.

        Returns:
            Span: A span.
        """
        if cells:
            start, end, style = self
            return Span(start, end + cells, style)
        else:
            return self

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: egv_verifier
function.description: Verify the current repair hypothesis with actual targeted assertions and relevant old behavior; return actionable evidence, never repair or submit.

function.name: get_status
function.description: Check active budget details (time, tool calls) and active patch details.

function.name: run_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command inside the repository sandbox.

        You can run any shell command (Python scripts, tests, git commands, etc.).
        The command runs in the repository workspace. No network access.

        Args:
            command: Shell command to execute (e.g., "pytest tests/", "python3 script.py").

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the contents of a file from the repository workspace.

        Supports reading specific line ranges using start_line and end_line (1-indexed).
        To avoid overwhelming the context window, large files are automatically truncated
        to a maximum number of lines (default: 150 lines).

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path within the workspace directory (e.g., "fastapi/main.py", "pyproject.toml").
            start_line: Optional starting line number (1-indexed, inclusive).
            end_line: Optional ending line number (1-indexed, inclusive).

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file content, line range, and truncation status.

function.name: edit_file
function.description:
Replace a contiguous block of text in an existing file.

        More token-efficient than write_file for targeted changes. Provide 2-4 lines of unique
        surrounding context in old_string to ensure an unambiguous match.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the target file.
            old_string: Text block to replace.
            new_string: Replacement text block.
            allow_multiple: Replace all occurrences of old_string if True.

        Returns:
            Dictionary containing file status, occurrences count, match strategy, and unified diff.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Create or overwrite a file in the workspace.

        Args:
            filepath: Relative path to the file to create or overwrite.
            content: Full content of the file.

function.name: submit_patch
function.description:
Capture the current working tree modifications as the agent's submission.

        This generates a unified git diff against the baseline commit. The agent
        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

function.name: egv_verifier
function.description: Verify the current repair hypothesis with actual targeted assertions and relevant old behavior; return actionable evidence, never repair or submit.

**Key Information & Analysis:**

*   Create a reproduction script to trigger the bug.
*   Implement and verify a fix.

        self,
        tokens: Iterable[Tuple[Any, StyleType]],
    ) -> None:
        """Append a sequence of (text, style) pairs to the text."""

        for content, style in tokens:

If `content` is not a string, `len(content)` might fail.

*   The agent has determined that the method needs to ensure `content` is a string to prevent crashes during length calculation or text joining.
*   The agent is weighing whether to implement a strict `TypeError` (consistent with `Text.append`) or a permissive cast to `str()`.
*   The agent is considering whether `strip_control_codes` should be applied to the content for consistency with other `Text` modification methods.

*   Finalize the implementation of the fix (validation vs. casting).
*   Verify if `strip_control_codes` should be integrated into `append_tokens`.
*   Create a formal reproduction test case to verify the fix.

*   The agent is considering whether `strip_control_codes` should be applied to the content for consistency with other `Text` modification methods.

        can submit multiple times; only the final submission is evaluated.

[model] said: The AI agent is working to resolve a reported exception in the `append_tokens` method of the `rich` library (Issue #3014).

**Key Information & Analysis:**
*   **Root Cause Identification:** The agent discovered that `append_tokens` (in `rich/text.py`) lacks input validation. If non-string `content` (e.g., `None`) is passed:
    1.  An immediate `TypeError` occurs when calling `len(content)` during offset calculation or span creation.
    2.  Even if that were bypassed, a delayed `TypeError` would occur when the `.plain` property is accessed, as it attempts to `"".join()` a list containing non-string elements.
*   **Consistency Check:** The agent noted that `Text.append` explicitly validates that inputs are strings (or `Text` objects) and raises a `TypeError` otherwise. `append_tokens` does not currently share this validation logic.
*   **Call Site Analysis:** Investigation of `rich/syntax.py` shows that `append_tokens` is primarily used with Pygments tokens. While these are typically strings, the lack of validation makes the public API vulnerable.
*   **Behavioral Discrepancy:** The agent observed that `append_tokens` does not strip control codes, whereas `Text.append` does, creating an inconsistency in how text length and content are handled.

**Decisions & Hypotheses:**
*   The agent has confirmed the bug with a reproduction test case, verifying that `None` as content triggers a `TypeError`.
*   The agent is weighing whether to implement a strict `TypeError` (to maintain consistency with `Text.append`) or a permissive cast to `str()`.
*   The agent is considering whether `strip_control_codes` should be integrated into `append_tokens` for consistency, while noting that this might impact performance for fast appending.

**Unresolved Tasks:**
*   Finalize the implementation of the fix (choosing between raising `TypeError` or casting to `str`).
*   Determine if `strip_control_codes` should be implemented within the loop.
*   Apply the fix to the codebase and verify it with the reproduction test case.
*   Submit the final patch.

[model] said: The AI agent is working to resolve a reported exception in the `append_tokens` method of the `rich` library (Issue #3014).

**Key Information & Analysis:**
*   **Root Cause Identification:** The agent discovered that `append_tokens` (in `rich/text.py`) lacks input validation. If non-string `content` (e.g., `None`) is passed:
    1.  An immediate `TypeError` occurs when calling `len(content)` during offset calculation or span creation.
    2.  Even if that were bypassed, a delayed `TypeError` would occur when the `.plain` property is accessed, as it attempts to `"".join()` a list containing non-string elements.
*   **Consistency Check:** The agent noted that `Text.append` explicitly validates that inputs are strings (or `Text` objects) and raises a `TypeError` otherwise. `append_tokens` does not currently share this validation logic.
*   **Call Site Analysis:** Investigation of `rich/syntax.py` shows that `append_tokens` is primarily used with Pygments tokens. While these are typically strings, the lack of validation makes the public API vulnerable.
*   **Behavioral Discrepancy:** The agent observed that `append_tokens` does not strip control codes, whereas `Text.append` does, creating an inconsistency in how text length and content are handled.

**Decisions & Hypotheses:**
*   The agent has confirmed the bug with a reproduction test case, verifying that `None` as content triggers a `TypeError`.
*   The agent is weighing whether to implement a strict `TypeError` (to maintain consistency with `Text.append`) or a permissive cast to `str()`.
*   The agent is considering whether `strip_control_codes` should be integrated into `append_tokens` for consistency, while noting that this might impact performance for fast appending.

*   Finalize the implementation of the fix (choosing between raising `TypeError` or casting to `str`).
*   Determine if `strip_control_codes` should be implemented within the loop.
*   Apply the fix to the codebase and verify it with the reproduction test case.
*   Submit the final patch.

[model] said: The AI agent is working to resolve a reported exception in the `append_tokens` method of the `rich` library (Issue #3014).

**Key Information & Analysis:**
*   **Root Cause Identification:** The agent discovered that `append_tokens` (in `rich/text.py`) lacks input validation. If non-string `content` (e.g., `None`) is passed:
    1.  An immediate `TypeError` occurs when calling `len(content)` during offset calculation or span creation.
    2.  Even if that were bypassed, a delayed `TypeError` would occur when the `.plain` property is accessed, as it attempts to `"".join()` a list containing non-string elements.

*   **Call Site Analysis:** Investigation of `rich/syntax.py` shows that `append_tokens` is primarily used with Pygments tokens. While these are typically strings, the lack of validation makes the public API vulnerable.
*   **Behavioral Discrepancy:** The agent observed that `append_tokens` does not strip control codes, whereas `Text.append` does, creating an inconsistency in how text length and content are handled.

**Decisions & Hypotheses:**
*   The agent has confirmed the bug with a reproduction test case, verifying that `None` as content triggers a `TypeError`.
*   The agent is weighing whether to implement a strict `TypeError` (to maintain consistency with `Text.append`) or a permissive cast to `str()`.
*   The agent is considering whether `strip_control_codes` should be integrated into `append_tokens` for consistency, while noting that this might impact performance for fast appending.

*   Finalize the implementation of the fix (choosing between raising `TypeError` or casting to `str`).
*   Determine if `strip_control_codes` should be implemented within the loop.
*   Apply the fix to the codebase and verify it with the reproduction test case.
*   Submit the final patch.

[model] said: The AI agent is working to resolve a reported exception in the `append_tokens` method of the `rich` library (Issue #3014).

**Key Information & Analysis:**
*   **Root Cause Identification:** The agent discovered that `append_tokens` (in `rich/text.py`) lacks input validation. If non-string `content` (e.g., `None`) is passed:
    1.  An immediate `TypeError` occurs when calling `len(content)` during offset calculation or span creation.
    2.  Even if that were bypassed, a delayed `TypeError` would occur when the `.plain` property is accessed, as it attempts to `"".join()` a list containing non-string elements.

*   **Call Site Analysis:** Investigation of `rich/syntax.py` shows that `append_tokens` is primarily used with Pygments tokens. While these are typically strings, the lack of validation makes the public API vulnerable.
*   **Behavioral Discrepancy:** The agent observed that `append_tokens` does not strip control codes, whereas `Text.append` does, creating an inconsistency in how text length and content are handled.

**Decisions & Hypotheses:**
*   The agent has confirmed the bug with a reproduction test case, verifying that `None` as content triggers a `TypeError`.
*   The agent is weighing whether to implement a strict `TypeError` (to maintain consistency with `Text.append`) or a permissive cast to `str()`.
*   The agent is considering whether `strip_control_codes` should be integrated into `append_tokens` for consistency, while noting that this might impact performance for fast appending.

*   Finalize the implementation of the fix (choosing between raising `TypeError` or casting to `str`).
*   Determine if `strip_control_codes` should be implemented within the loop.
*   Apply the fix to the codebase and verify it with the reproduction test case.

class Span(NamedTuple):
    """A marked up region in some text."""

    start: int
    """Span start index."""
    end: int
    """Span end index."""
    style: Union[str, Style]
    """Style associated with the span."""

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Span({self.start}, {self.end}, {self.style!r})"

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return self.end > self.start

    def split(self, offset: int) -> Tuple["Span", Optional["Span"]]:
        """Split a span in to 2 from a given offset."""

        if offset < self.start:
            return self, None
        if offset >= self.end:
            return self, None

        start, end, style = self
        span1 = Span(start, min(end, offset), style)
        span2 = Span(span1.end, end, style)
        return span1, span2

    def move(self, offset: int) -> "Span":
        """Move start and end by a given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): Number of characters to add to start and end.

        Returns:
            TextSpan: A new TextSpan with adjusted position.
        """
        start, end, style = self
        return Span(start + offset, end + offset, style)

    def right_crop(self, offset: int) -> "Span":
        """Crop the span at the given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): A value between start and end.

        Returns:
            Span: A new (possibly smaller) span.
        """
        start, end, style = self
        if offset >= end:
            return self
        return Span(start, min(offset, end), style)

class Span(NamedTuple):
    """A marked up region in some text."""

    start: int
    """Span start index."""
    end: int
    """Span end index."""
    style: Union[str, Style]
    """Style associated with the span."""

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Span({self.start}, {self.end}, {self.style!r})"

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return self.end > self.start

    def split(self, offset: int) -> Tuple["Span", Optional["Span"]]:
        """Split a span in to 2 from a given offset."""

        if offset < self.start:
            return self, None
        if offset >= self.end:
            return self, None

        start, end, style = self
        span1 = Span(start, min(end, offset), style)
        span2 = Span(span1.end, end, style)
        return span1, span2

        """Move start and end by a given offset.

        Args:

        start, end, style = self
        return Span(start + offset, end + offset, style)

        """Crop the span at the given offset.

class Span(NamedTuple):
    """A marked up region in some text."""

    start: int
    """Span start index."""
    end: int
    """Span end index."""
    style: Union[str, Style]
    """Style associated with the span."""

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Span({self.start}, {self.end}, {self.style!r})"

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return self.end > self.start

    def split(self, offset: int) -> Tuple["Span", Optional["Span"]]:
        """Split a span in to 2 from a given offset."""

        if offset < self.start:
            return self, None
        if offset >= self.end:
            return self, None

        start, end, style = self
        span1 = Span(start, min(end, offset), style)
        span2 = Span(span1.end, end, style)
        return span1, span2

        """Move start and end by a given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): Number of characters to add to start and end.

        Returns:
            TextSpan: A new TextSpan with adjusted position.

        start, end, style = self
        return Span(start + offset, end + offset, style)

        """Crop the span at the given offset.

        Returns:
            Span: A new (possibly smaller) span.
        """
        start, end, style = self
        if offset >= end:

        return Span(start, min(offset, end), style)

class Span(NamedTuple):
    """A marked up region in some text."""

    start: int
    """Span start index."""
    end: int
    """Span end index."""
    style: Union[str, Style]
    """Style associated with the span."""

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Span({self.start}, {self.end}, {self.style!r})"

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return self.end > self.start

    def split(self, offset: int) -> Tuple["Span", Optional["Span"]]:
        """Split a span in to 2 from a given offset."""

        if offset < self.start:
            return self, None
        if offset >= self.end:
            return self, None

        start, end, style = self
        span1 = Span(start, min(end, offset), style)
        span2 = Span(span1.end, end, style)
        return span1, span2

    def move(self, offset: int) -> "Span":
        """Move start and end by a given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): Number of characters to add to start and end.

        Returns:
            TextSpan: A new TextSpan with adjusted position.
        """
        start, end, style = self
        return Span(start + offset, end + offset, style)

    def right_crop(self, offset: int) -> "Span":
        """Crop the span at the given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): A value between start and end.

        Returns:

        """

        if offset >= end:

class Span(NamedTuple):
    """A marked up region in some text."""

    start: int
    """Span start index."""
    end: int
    """Span end index."""
    style: Union[str, Style]
    """Style associated with the span."""

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Span({self.start}, {self.end}, {self.style!r})"

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        return self.end > self.start

    def split(self, offset: int) -> Tuple["Span", Optional["Span"]]:
        """Split a span in to 2 from a given offset."""

        if offset < self.start:
            return self, None
        if offset >= self.end:
            return self, None

        start, end, style = self
        span1 = Span(start, min(end, offset), style)
        span2 = Span(span1.end, end, style)
        return span1, span2

        """Move start and end by a given offset.

        Args:
            offset (int): Number of characters to add to start and end.

        Returns:
            TextSpan: A new TextSpan with adjusted position.

        start, end, style = self
        return Span(start + offset, end + offset, style)

        """Crop the span at the given offset.
